races.title: State House, District 104
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Brandon Lofton
cands.bio: Democrat representing North Carolina House District 104 (southwest Mecklenburg County) since January 2019. Partner at the law firm Robinson Bradshaw, focusing on public finance. Began his legal career at the civil rights firm Ferguson Stein Chambers. UNC Chapel Hill graduate (2001) with an NYU law degree (2004).

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina (listed among his 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations)

cands.gaps: We could not find where Brandon Lofton was born or what town he grew up in, or when or whether he moved to North Carolina; his statements about NC public schools are the only evidence of his upbringing. We found no documented positions on data centers, development or growth, and nothing on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, or gun policy. We found no pages showing a specific action he took on any of those topics. The pages did not show his stance on school vouchers or charters. The legislative sponsorship list on his Ballotpedia page was empty in the copy we read. No controversies or foreign ties appeared in the pages we had. His campaign site describes his bills and positions, but those are his own claims and were not checked against legislative records.

local.label: Roots 90: In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey he called himself "the product of North Carolina public schools" and referred to "the North Carolina schools of my childhood," which shows he was raised in the state; his birthplace was not found.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2019 (seven years). He is a public finance lawyer who advises local governments, universities and nonprofits on financing capital projects, and he began as a civil rights lawyer. Before the legislature he chaired Charlotte's Disparity Study Advisory Committee.
qual.why: Years of prior legislative service, including seats on the House Finance Committee, plus a law career centered on public finance, fit the work of writing law and budgets. Board and advisory roles and committee seats were not counted toward the score.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he is working to increase teacher pay and to fully fund public schools, and that he sponsored or cosponsored bills to restore master's pay for teachers. The pages say nothing about his position on vouchers, charters or school choice.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he stood against legislative efforts to violate women's constitutional right to control their reproductive health decisions, and that he is working to protect women's right to make their own healthcare decisions.

cands.name: Trina Boyd
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina House District 104 in 2026. She advanced without a primary and lost the general election to incumbent Brandon Lofton (D). In 2022 she ran in the Democratic primary for Mecklenburg County Board of Commissioners At-Large and did not advance. No office held is documented.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Trina Boyd was born or raised, or when she came to North Carolina. We could not find her occupation, education or work history. She has held no elected office. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026, and we found no campaign website, questionnaire or interview stating her positions. We found nothing documenting her actions or positions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. We found no news coverage of controversies, no foreign ties and no endorsements; Ballotpedia says it identified none for 2026.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Ballotpedia lists two campaigns: the 2022 Democratic primary for Mecklenburg County Commissioners At-Large (9.9%, did not advance) and the 2026 run for NC House District 104. It gives no occupation, career or office held.
qual.why: The available page gives no job history and shows no office held, so the background can't be scored.
